Quota-Resilient Harvester (24h Cache TTL + Exponential Backoff)

🏗️ Solution Architecture (Local Cache Mode & Serverless GCP Mode)

Inspired by aws-services.info/arch.html and builder.aws.com/build/capabilities, this solution is engineered to run both 100% locally on your workstation (with a once-a-day background refresh & static HTML/JSON cache) and as a serverless Google Cloud architecture at near-zero cost (~$0.78/month).

🛡️ Quota & Rate-Limit Protection Architecture

  • Daily 24-Hour Cache TTL (`data/cache/gcp_catalog.json`): All user searches, region lookups, matrix comparisons, and CLI queries are served 100% from local static HTML and cached JSON. Upstream GCP endpoints are only queried once every 24 hours (or when explicitly forced via --force).
  • Token-Bucket Rate Limiting: Outbound requests during the daily harvest are paced through a thread-safe token-bucket rate limiter (default 15 requests/sec across 8 bounded worker threads) to prevent burst quota exhaustion on discovery.googleapis.com.
  • Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter & Retry-After Parsing: Any HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, 403 Rate Limit Exceeded, or 5xx response automatically honors the server's Retry-After header or backs off using random.uniform(0.5 * base * 2^attempt, base * 2^attempt) up to 5 attempts.
  • Per-API Disk Checkpointing & Graceful Stale-Cache Fallback: Every Discovery REST spec (data/cache/discovery/{api}_{version}.json) is atomically written to disk as soon as it arrives. If network connectivity drops mid-run, re-running resumes instantly without re-fetching completed specs, and falls back to the last known good cached spec if an upstream endpoint is temporarily unreachable.

☁️ Equivalent Serverless Google Cloud Production Architecture & Cost

Just like aws-services.info/arch.html uses ECR + Lambda + EventBridge + S3 + CloudFront + WAF, here is the 1-to-1 Google Cloud Serverless mapping and monthly cost breakdown:
